sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的 DealBook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上免费直播部分精选采访，供所有人观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得一个月的免费访问权限，畅读我们所有的报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today, in back-to-back votes, the Senate has just approved a bipartisan infrastructure bill and a partisan budget plan.
sentences.zh: 今天，参议院接连进行了两场投票，刚刚批准了一项两党基础设施法案和一项党派预算计划。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague, Emily Cochran, about the complicated relationship between the two and what that tells us about how Washington now works.
sentences.zh: 我和我的同事艾米丽·科克伦谈到了这两者之间复杂的关系，以及这反映出华盛顿目前的运作方式。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, August 12th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月12日，星期四。

sentences.en: Hi, Emily.
sentences.zh: 你好，艾米丽。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: What kind of incredibly small, confined space are you in?
sentences.zh: 你现在待在一个多么狭小、封闭的空间里啊？

sentences.en: This is one of the booths in the House Press Gallery.
sentences.zh: 这是众议院新闻发布厅里的隔间之一。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: It has, like, nice padding.
sentences.zh: 它有那种不错的衬垫。

sentences.en: I assumed that was helpful for recording purposes.
sentences.zh: 我以为这对录音很有帮助。

sentences.en: So you have found a quiet corner of the universe on the House side.
sentences.zh: 所以你在众议院那边找到了宇宙中一个安静的角落。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, Emily, walk us through what has happened so far this week, not on the House side of the Capitol, but over on the Senate side.
sentences.zh: 那么，艾米丽，请带我们回顾一下本周到目前为止发生的事情，不是在国会大厦的众议院那边，而是在参议院那边。

sentences.en: So...
sentences.zh: 好的……

sentences.en: It's been a long and winding road.
sentences.zh: 这是一段漫长而曲折的道路。

sentences.en: On Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 在周二。

sentences.en: But we have persisted, and now we have arrived.
sentences.zh: 但我们坚持了下来，现在我们终于到达了终点。

sentences.en: After one final round of speeches and preemptive congratulations...
sentences.zh: 在最后一轮演讲和预先的祝贺之后……

sentences.en: The Senate's about to make history.
sentences.zh: 参议院即将创造历史。

sentences.en: And we've heard over the years, in fact, over the decades, about the need for us to fix our infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 多年来，事实上几十年来，我们一直听到关于需要修复基础设施的呼声。

sentences.en: Senators started to come to the floor for the final vote on a $1 trillion infrastructure package.
sentences.zh: 参议员们开始进入议事厅，对一项1万亿美元的基础设施方案进行最终投票。

sentences.en: Clerk will call the roll.
sentences.zh: 书记员将进行点名。

sentences.en: Ms. Baldwin, Mr. Barrasso, Mr. Bennett, Mrs. Blackburn...
sentences.zh: 鲍德温女士、巴拉索先生、贝内特先生、布莱克本夫人……

sentences.en: The largest single infusion of federal funds in infrastructure in more than a decade.
sentences.zh: 这是十多年来联邦政府在基础设施方面最大规模的一次资金注入。

sentences.en: Mr. McConnell, Mr. Menendez...
sentences.zh: 麦康奈尔先生、梅嫩德斯先生……

sentences.en: There was an expectation that it would pass, because it had cleared so many hurdles.
sentences.zh: 人们普遍预期它会通过，因为它已经扫清了太多的障碍。

sentences.en: Republicans had again and again crossed over to join Democrats in supporting this package.
sentences.zh: 共和党人一次又一次地跨越党派界限，加入民主党人的行列支持这项方案。

sentences.en: But this is the final vote.
sentences.zh: 但这是最终投票。

sentences.en: This is when it matters.
sentences.zh: 这是关键时刻。

sentences.en: This is, I support it becoming law.
sentences.zh: 这就是我支持它成为法律的时刻。

sentences.en: At the end...
sentences.zh: 最后……

sentences.en: On this vote, the yeas are 69.
sentences.zh: 本次投票结果，赞成票69张。

sentences.en: The nays are 30.
sentences.zh: 反对票30张。

sentences.en: 19 Republicans and all 50 Democrats passed the bill.
sentences.zh: 19名共和党人和全部50名民主党人通过了该法案。

sentences.en: The bill, as amended, is passed.
sentences.zh: 该法案经修正后获得通过。

sentences.en: And when it passed, there was sort of this moment of silence.
sentences.zh: 当它通过时，现场出现了一种沉默的时刻。

sentences.en: It almost felt like the room couldn't believe that after all these weeks, it was over.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像整个议事厅都不敢相信，在经历了这么多周之后，一切终于结束了。

sentences.en: It passed.
sentences.zh: 它通过了。

sentences.en: It was through the Senate.
sentences.zh: 它在参议院获得了通过。

sentences.en: Once again, congratulations to all of those who worked hard, so hard, on this very significant and very important bill.
sentences.zh: 再次祝贺所有为这项意义重大、非常重要的法案付出辛勤努力的人们。

sentences.en: So, Emily, tell us exactly what is in this $1 trillion infrastructure bill.
sentences.zh: 那么，艾米丽，请告诉我们这项1万亿美元的基础设施法案到底包含什么内容。

sentences.en: So, in the $1 trillion package, the biggest thing is that there's about $550 billion in new federal funds.
sentences.zh: 在这个1万亿美元的方案中，最重要的一点是其中约有5500亿美元是新的联邦资金。

sentences.en: So, it's not just continuing and maintaining existing programs for roads, highways, and the like.
sentences.zh: 所以，这不仅仅是延续和维护现有的道路、高速公路等项目。

sentences.en: It's a ton of new money that can be distributed across the country.
sentences.zh: 这是一大笔可以分配到全国各地的新资金。

sentences.en: For the first time, there's $65 billion for broadband, a huge sum of money to help ensure Internet access.
sentences.zh: 这是首次为宽带投入650亿美元，这是一笔巨款，旨在帮助确保互联网接入。

sentences.en: There's $110 billion for roads and highways.
sentences.zh: 其中有1100亿美元用于道路和高速公路。

sentences.en: There's money in there to help address lead and water, so addressing lead pipes.
sentences.zh: 其中还有资金用于解决铅和水的问题，即处理铅管。

sentences.en: And one of the most notable things was this is likely the largest amount of money for climate resiliency that the federal government has approved.
sentences.zh: 最值得注意的事情之一是，这很可能是联邦政府批准的用于气候适应能力的最大一笔资金。

sentences.en: So, it's helping to modernize the nation's electric grid.
sentences.zh: 它有助于实现国家电网的现代化。

sentences.en: It's helping federal agencies not just counter the toll of climate change and the toll that these natural disasters bring upon communities, but helping them prepare for it.
sentences.zh: 它不仅能帮助联邦机构应对气候变化带来的损失以及这些自然灾害给社区造成的损害，还能帮助他们为此做好准备。

sentences.en: You know, maybe helping communities relocate, if that's an option,
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许是帮助社区搬迁，如果这是一个选择的话，

sentences.en: helping shore up seawalls and basic infrastructure that could help communities just withstand the natural disasters better.
sentences.zh: 帮助加固海堤和基础基础设施，这些都能帮助社区更好地抵御自然灾害。

sentences.en: That sounds like an enormous piece of legislation.
sentences.zh: 听起来这是一项庞大的立法。

sentences.en: It's pretty significant.
sentences.zh: 确实意义重大。

sentences.en: It's something that, for decades, presidents have sought.
sentences.zh: 这是几十年来历任总统一直寻求的目标。

sentences.en: Barack Obama, Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 巴拉克·奥巴马、唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: This has always been sort of the elusive last bipartisan issue standing that could get people to come out of their corners, come together,
sentences.zh: 这一直被认为是最后剩下的、难以捉摸的两党议题，它能促使人们走出各自的立场，团结起来，

sentences.en: and really deliver significant aid to their communities.
sentences.zh: 并真正为他们的社区提供重要的援助。

sentences.en: So far, it hasn't happened for a variety of different reasons, but this became the moment that it was possible.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，由于各种不同的原因，这还没有实现，但现在成为了可能。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, let's talk about that, how this actually happened, and how Democrats were able to pull this off and bring those 19 Republicans along to vote for this.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们来谈谈这件事，它是如何真正发生的，以及民主党人是如何做到这一点，并争取到那19名共和党人投票支持的。

sentences.en: So, I think it started after President Biden laid down his marker for an infrastructure plan.
sentences.zh: 我认为这始于拜登总统为基础设施计划设定目标之后。

sentences.en: Early in the spring, after the pandemic relief package passed, the president turned toward infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 春季早些时候，在疫情救助方案通过后，总统将目光转向了基础设施。

sentences.en: He had said over the campaign that there was a priority, and he put out his own plan.
sentences.zh: 他在竞选期间曾表示这是一个优先事项，并提出了他自己的计划。

sentences.en: It was a $2.3 trillion plan, so more than double the bill that we saw passed on Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 那是一个2.3万亿美元的计划，是我们在周二看到通过的法案的两倍多。

sentences.en: And for moderate Democrats who are determined to prove that the Senate can work,
sentences.zh: 对于那些决心证明参议院能够运作的温和派民主党人来说，

sentences.en: who are determined to sort of hold off some of their colleagues who perhaps are looking to just cut out Republicans altogether,
sentences.zh: 对于那些决心抵制某些可能只想完全排除共和党人的同事的民主党人来说，

sentences.en: this was an opportunity to prove to those colleagues and their voters that the Senate can be bipartisan.
sentences.zh: 这是一个向那些同事和选民证明参议院可以实现两党合作的机会。

sentences.en: So, in April or so, Rob Portman, who's a retiring Republican from Ohio, and Kyrsten Sinema, who's a first-year Democrat from Arizona,
sentences.zh: 所以，大约在4月份，来自俄亥俄州的即将退休的共和党人罗布·波特曼和来自亚利桑那州的第一任民主党人克里斯汀·西内马，

sentences.en: start talking about the ways that they could possibly reach a compromise on an infrastructure package.
sentences.zh: 开始讨论他们可能在基础设施方案上达成妥协的方式。

sentences.en: And over the next few weeks, they sort of get together this core group of 10 senators.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几周里，他们组建了一个由10名参议员组成的核心小组。

sentences.en: Five Republicans and five Democrats who start quietly working on, you know, possible ways to bring down the price tag and sort of shape the legislation more to their liking.
sentences.zh: 5名共和党人和5名民主党人开始悄悄地研究，你知道，降低价格标签的可能方法，并根据他们的喜好塑造立法。

sentences.en: And was there thinking that if they could get this infrastructure proposal to a place of their liking, the liking of moderates from swing states, Arizona and Ohio,
sentences.zh: 当时是否有一种想法，即如果他们能将这项基础设施提案调整到他们喜欢的程度，即亚利桑那州和俄亥俄州这些摇摆州温和派喜欢的程度，

sentences.en: that they could possibly get it to the liking of the entire Senate?
sentences.zh: 他们是否可能让整个参议院都满意？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: At a time when Washington seems broken, this group of members behind me came together, along with others, and decided we were going to do something great for our country.
sentences.zh: 在华盛顿似乎陷入瘫痪的时候，我身后的这群议员与其他议员走到了一起，决定我们要为我们的国家做一些伟大的事情。

sentences.en: For Senator Portman, he's a longtime creature of Washington.
sentences.zh: 对于波特曼参议员来说，他是一位长期的华盛顿老手。

sentences.en: He served in the Bush administration at the top levels.
sentences.zh: 他曾在布什政府担任高级职务。

sentences.en: He was in the House.
sentences.zh: 他曾在众议院任职。

sentences.en: Now he's in the Senate on his final term.
sentences.zh: 现在他正处于参议院的最后一个任期。

sentences.en: He carries a lot of respect among his Republican colleagues.
sentences.zh: 他在共和党同事中享有很高的声望。

sentences.en: With this, I'd like to turn to Senator Sinema.
sentences.zh: 借此机会，我想请西内马参议员发言。

sentences.en: Thanks so much, Rob.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，罗布。

sentences.en: You know, I first want to echo what Rob said about the dedication of this group.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我首先想呼应罗布关于这个小组奉献精神的评价。

sentences.en: And for Senator Sinema, who's still in her first term, this was not only a chance to shape the package, narrow the scope in a way that reflected her ideology a little more.
sentences.zh: 对于仍处于第一任期的西内马参议员来说，这不仅是一个塑造方案的机会，也是一个以更符合她意识形态的方式缩小范围的机会。

sentences.en: It was an opportunity for someone in their first term to assert themselves.
sentences.zh: 对于一个处于第一任期的人来说，这是一个展示自己的机会。

sentences.en: And she's a senator from Arizona.
sentences.zh: 她是来自亚利桑那州的参议员。

sentences.en: She's often referenced the late John McCain, who, while a Republican, did sometimes buck his party, most notably with the attempt to repeal the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 她经常提到已故的约翰·麦凯恩，他虽然是共和党人，但有时确实会反抗自己的党派，最著名的是在试图废除《平价医疗法案》时。

sentences.en: She cited him as a role model.
sentences.zh: 她将他视为榜样。

sentences.en: And this was an opportunity to sort of carry on that legacy.
sentences.zh: 这是一个延续那种遗产的机会。

sentences.en: Each of us are deeply committed to demonstrating to the country and to the world that our government can work, and it can work for the people of the United States of America.
sentences.zh: 我们每个人都坚定地致力于向全国和全世界证明，我们的政府能够运作，并且能够为美利坚合众国的人民服务。

sentences.en: So, ultimately, the White House begins negotiating with this group in earneSt.
sentences.zh: 最终，白宫开始与这个小组进行认真的谈判。

sentences.en: There were hours after hours after hours of meetings on Capitol Hill where top White House officials
sentences.zh: 在国会大厦，白宫高层官员进行了数小时又数小时的会议，

sentences.en: and this group of 10 senators bounced from room to room to room to room, haggling over the details of this plan.
sentences.zh: 这10名参议员小组在各个房间之间穿梭，为该计划的细节讨价还价。

sentences.en: So, night after night, sometimes close to midnight, they would be in basement hideaways that were so small,
sentences.zh: 所以，夜复一夜，有时接近午夜，他们会待在地下室里非常狭小的隐蔽房间里，

sentences.en: aides had to bring in extra fans to make sure that the room didn't overheat.
sentences.zh: 助手们不得不搬来额外的风扇，以确保房间不会过热。

sentences.en: Senator Sinema actually broke her foot running a marathon and was quite literally on some form of crutches, hobbling across the Capitol from one room to another.
sentences.zh: 西内马参议员实际上在跑马拉松时摔断了脚，确实是拄着某种拐杖，一瘸一拐地穿过国会大厦从一个房间走到另一个房间。

sentences.en: And so, we would end up chasing them all over the Capitol just to figure out what was going on.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们最终会在国会大厦到处追着他们，只是为了弄清楚发生了什么。

sentences.en: Are they actually making progress?
sentences.zh: 他们真的在取得进展吗？

sentences.en: And in these small, hot hideaway rooms, what exactly are senators Sinema and Portman doing to try to get this done?
sentences.zh: 在这些狭小、炎热的隐蔽房间里，西内马和波特曼参议员到底在做什么来试图完成这项工作？

sentences.en: So, the two of them are not only coordinating and leading these meetings for the group of senators, but they're also, in a way, holding off the extremes of both of their parties
sentences.zh: 他们两人不仅在协调和领导这些参议员小组会议，而且在某种程度上，他们还在抵制各自党派的极端分子，

sentences.en: who don't necessarily want to embrace this deal.
sentences.zh: 那些人并不一定想接受这项协议。

sentences.en: Most notably for Senator Portman, that entails taking on former President Trump, who couldn't get his own infrastructure deal done in his term and is now telling Republicans
sentences.zh: 对于波特曼参议员来说，最值得注意的是，这需要对抗前总统特朗普，他在任期内没能完成自己的基础设施协议，现在正告诉共和党人

sentences.en: to stay away from this deal.
sentences.zh: 远离这项协议。

sentences.en: He's throwing all sorts of insults at the Republicans who have signaled some support.
sentences.zh: 他向那些表示支持的共和党人抛出了各种侮辱。

sentences.en: He's threatening to challenge anyone who votes for it.
sentences.zh: 他威胁要挑战任何投票支持它的人。

sentences.en: And at one point, Portman even calls President Trump and makes the case to him that he should actually be supporting this bill
sentences.zh: 有一次，波特曼甚至打电话给特朗普总统，向他陈述他实际上应该支持这项法案的理由，

sentences.en: because had he not proposed his own big infrastructure package,
sentences.zh: 因为如果他当初没有提出自己的大型基础设施方案，

sentences.en: Republicans wouldn't even be open to the size that they were currently discussing.
sentences.zh: 共和党人甚至不会对他们目前讨论的规模持开放态度。

sentences.en: Ah, trying to kill him with kindness.
sentences.zh: 啊，试图用善意感化他。

sentences.en: He was definitely using flattery.
sentences.zh: 他绝对是在使用奉承手段。

sentences.en: So, after endless late-night meetings, pizza, wine, endless Zoom calls and text message chains,
sentences.zh: 所以，在无数次深夜会议、披萨、红酒、无休止的 Zoom 通话和短信链之后，

sentences.en: Portman, Sinema, and this group of senators finally unveils this 2,702-page bill that the Senate ultimately passes on Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 波特曼、西内马和这个参议员小组终于公布了这份2702页的法案，参议院最终在周二通过了它。

sentences.en: Right, which, as you said, passed in not just a bipartisan way, but in a remarkably bipartisan way with nearly half of Senate Republicans supporting it,
sentences.zh: 没错，正如你所说，它不仅以两党合作的方式通过，而且是以一种非常显著的两党合作方式通过的，近一半的参议院共和党人支持它，

sentences.en: including the very partisan Senate leader for Republicans, Mitch McConnell.
sentences.zh: 包括共和党内非常党派化的参议院领袖米奇·麦康奈尔。

sentences.en: But that is just the Senate side, and this infrastructure bill is not yet across the final finish line.
sentences.zh: 但这只是参议院方面，这项基础设施法案还没有到达最终的终点线。

sentences.en: Far from it.
sentences.zh: 远非如此。

sentences.en: Because in order to win the support of progressives and liberals who said this bill wasn't enough, that more needed to be done,
sentences.zh: 因为为了赢得那些认为该法案不够充分、需要做更多工作的进步派和自由派的支持，

sentences.en: Senator Sinema agreed to go along with a much more partisan process that could undermine the very bipartisanship this bill represents.
sentences.zh: 西内马参议员同意进行一个更具党派色彩的程序，这可能会破坏该法案所代表的两党合作精神。

sentences.en: And that process began immediately after the bill passed.
sentences.zh: 而那个程序在法案通过后立即开始了。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费探索《时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用程序中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall, to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 一个月的时间去深入了解付费墙后的内容，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《时报》应用程序，并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So Emily, what is this second, far more partisan process you mentioned, and how exactly does it relate to the bipartisan infrastructure bill that was just passed in the Senate?
sentences.zh: 那么艾米丽，你提到的第二个更具党派色彩的程序是什么？它与刚刚在参议院通过的两党基础设施法案到底有什么关系？

sentences.en: So Democrats who control the House, the Senate, and the White House have always wanted more.
sentences.zh: 控制众议院、参议院和白宫的民主党人一直想要更多。

sentences.en: They wanted more climate provisions.
sentences.zh: 他们想要更多的气候条款。

sentences.en: They wanted more funding to push the boundaries of what has traditionally been defined as infrastructure, what President Biden and others have started calling human infrastructure,
sentences.zh: 他们想要更多的资金来突破传统上被定义为基础设施的界限，即拜登总统和其他人开始称之为“人力基础设施”的东西，

sentences.en: child care, home care, education.
sentences.zh: 儿童保育、家庭护理、教育。

sentences.en: All of those ultimately got left out of the bipartisan deal because those were never going to get Republican votes.
sentences.zh: 所有这些最终都被排除在两党协议之外，因为这些永远无法获得共和党的投票。

sentences.en: Right, because they're seen as social programs and often progressive social programs rather than traditional brick-and-mortar infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为它们被视为社会项目，通常是进步的社会项目，而不是传统的实体基础设施。

sentences.en: Yes, and Democrats also had very strong feelings about how to pay for the bill, namely by increasing taxes on wealthy people and wealthy corporations
sentences.zh: 是的，民主党人对于如何支付该法案的费用也有非常强烈的看法，即通过增加对富人和富裕企业的税收，

sentences.en: and undoing key elements of the 2017 tax law, which only Republicans supported and were not going to support undoing.
sentences.zh: 并撤销2017年税法中的关键要素，该法案只有共和党人支持，他们不会支持撤销。

sentences.en: So progressives in both the Senate and the House, but particularly in the House, made very clear that they would not support a smaller bipartisan agreement
sentences.zh: 所以参议院和众议院的进步派，特别是众议院的进步派，非常明确地表示他们不会支持一个规模较小的两党协议。

sentences.en: unless more of their priorities, more of these priorities, were passed in a separate package, passed in a process that is called budget reconciliation.
sentences.zh: 除非他们的更多优先事项，即这些优先事项中的更多内容，能通过一个单独的一揽子计划，通过一种被称为“预算协调”的程序获得通过。

sentences.en: A bipartisan agreement will not pass unless we have a reconciliation bill that also passes.
sentences.zh: 除非我们同时也通过一项协调法案，否则两党协议将无法通过。

sentences.en: There simply won't be the votes for it in the House unless, unless we have at the same time the reconciliation bill that has been passed.
sentences.zh: 除非我们同时通过那项协调法案，否则众议院根本不会有足够的票数支持它。

sentences.en: A majority of House progressives have repeatedly and explicitly said that they will not support the bipartisan infrastructure deal
sentences.zh: 大多数众议院进步派议员已多次明确表示，他们不会支持这项两党基础设施协议，

sentences.en: until that second, much bigger, much more expensive reconciliation package clears the Senate.
sentences.zh: 直到那第二个规模更大、成本更高的协调方案在参议院获得通过。

sentences.en: We've been very clear we've got five priorities.
sentences.zh: 我们已经非常明确地表示，我们有五项优先事项。

sentences.en: If those priorities aren't met, there is not going to be a piece of legislation that passes.
sentences.zh: 如果这些优先事项得不到满足，就不会有任何法案获得通过。

sentences.en: And of course, you know, it's not just progressives.
sentences.zh: 当然，你知道，不仅仅是进步派这么想。

sentences.en: Now the Speaker has said the same thing.
sentences.zh: 现在议长也表达了同样的看法。

sentences.en: And so far, Speaker Nancy Pelosi has said that that's what she plans to do, that she won't hold a vote on the bipartisan infrastructure deal until she sees the second package.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，议长南希·佩洛西表示她打算这样做，即在看到第二个方案之前，她不会对两党基础设施协议进行投票。

sentences.en: What's different about budget reconciliation is that you don't need 60 votes the way you do for the bipartisan infrastructure bill or any other piece of legislation.
sentences.zh: 预算协调的不同之处在于，你不需要像两党基础设施法案或任何其他法案那样需要60票。

sentences.en: You just need 50.
sentences.zh: 你只需要50票。

sentences.en: So in essence, Democrats don't need Republican votes for this package.
sentences.zh: 因此，从本质上讲，民主党人不需要共和党人的投票来通过这个方案。

sentences.en: They just need to stay united and push it through all on their own.
sentences.zh: 他们只需要保持团结，完全靠自己推动它通过。

sentences.en: So there's kind of a threat being issued here from progressives, especially in the House, that they won't do their part to get the bipartisan infrastructure bill turned into law
sentences.zh: 所以进步派，特别是在众议院的进步派，发出了一种威胁，即他们不会尽自己的一份力让两党基础设施法案成为法律，

sentences.en: unless they get what they want in budget reconciliation.
sentences.zh: 除非他们在预算协调中得到他们想要的东西。

sentences.en: So they have kind of tethered these two processes together and said we won't do one without the other.
sentences.zh: 所以他们实际上把这两个程序捆绑在了一起，并表示没有对方，他们就不会做其中任何一个。

sentences.en: It's essentially a really precarious bargain between progressives and moderate Democrats.
sentences.zh: 这本质上是进步派和温和派民主党人之间一种非常不稳定的交易。

sentences.en: The House needs to pass this for it to become law.
sentences.zh: 众议院需要通过这项法案，它才能成为法律。

sentences.en: And in the House where there's a really slim majority, you have progressives saying the only way you get our votes is if we get this much bigger partisan budget package.
sentences.zh: 在众议院，由于多数优势非常微弱，进步派表示，要获得我们的投票，唯一的办法就是我们必须得到这个规模大得多的党派预算方案。

sentences.en: And in the Senate, that means every single Democrat needs to be on board.
sentences.zh: 而在参议院，这意味着每一位民主党人都必须参与其中。

sentences.en: So despite this long road we've taken, we have finally, finally reached the finish line.
sentences.zh: 所以尽管我们经历了漫长的道路，我们终于，终于到达了终点线。

sentences.en: Of course, we Democrats believe we need to do much more.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们民主党人认为我们需要做得更多。

sentences.en: The bipartisan infrastructure bill is a very significant bill.
sentences.zh: 两党基础设施法案是一项非常重要的法案。

sentences.en: But our country has other very significant, very important challenges.
sentences.zh: 但我们的国家还有其他非常重大、非常重要的挑战。

sentences.en: And so at the same time that the Senate passes this bipartisan bill,
sentences.zh: 因此，在参议院通过这项两党法案的同时，

sentences.en: Senator Chuck Schumer, the majority leader, sets up a vote to move forward with this reconciliation process.
sentences.zh: 多数党领袖查克·舒默参议员安排了一次投票，以推进这一协调程序。

sentences.en: We are moving on to a second track, which will make generational transformation in these areas.
sentences.zh: 我们正在进入第二轨道，这将使这些领域发生代际变革。

sentences.en: With a $3.5 trillion price tag and a plan to provide for all of the tax increases, health care, education, and climate provisions that Democrats want.
sentences.zh: 该计划耗资3.5万亿美元，旨在为民主党人想要的所有增税、医疗保健、教育和气候条款提供资金。

sentences.en: The two-track strategy is proceeding full steam ahead.
sentences.zh: 双轨战略正在全速推进。

sentences.en: So this is the second process.
sentences.zh: 这就是第二个程序。

sentences.en: And it's about three times the cost of the bipartisan infrastructure bill.
sentences.zh: 它的成本大约是两党基础设施法案的三倍。

sentences.en: So it's an enormous undertaking.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一项巨大的工程。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And it's far from over.
sentences.zh: 而且远未结束。

sentences.en: Democrats, after prevailing over a really long, painful amendment process, did ultimately pass this budget blueprint, this $3.5 trillion blueprint, just before 4 a.m.
sentences.zh: 民主党人在经历了一个非常漫长、痛苦的修正案程序后，最终在周三凌晨4点前通过了这个预算蓝图，这个3.5万亿美元的蓝图，所有民主党人保持团结，面对共和党人的一致反对。

sentences.en: Wednesday morning with all Democrats staying united over unanimous Republican opposition.
sentences.zh: 周三凌晨。

sentences.en: But we've already heard from a couple of key moderates, namely Joe Manchin of West Virginia and Senator Sinema,
sentences.zh: 但我们已经听到几位关键的温和派人士，即西弗吉尼亚州的乔·曼钦和西内马参议员的声音，

sentences.en: saying that while they were okay beginning the process of considering a package that could be this large,
sentences.zh: 他们表示，虽然他们同意开始审议一个可能如此庞大的方案，

sentences.en: they may not ultimately be comfortable with a package of that size.
sentences.zh: 但他们最终可能对如此规模的方案感到不安。

sentences.en: So there's a lot to iron out.
sentences.zh: 所以还有很多细节需要敲定。

sentences.en: They have to actually come to agreement on the details of this package and hammer out the specifics of what the price tag and the policies are ultimately going to be.
sentences.zh: 他们必须就该方案的细节达成一致，并敲定最终的价格标签和政策的具体内容。

sentences.en: And with no wiggle room in the Senate, that's going to be a pretty heavy lift for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 由于参议院没有任何回旋余地，这对民主党人来说将是一项相当艰巨的任务。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Let's presume for a moment, Emily, that Democrats can ultimately get on the same page when it comes to this two-pronged process.
sentences.zh: 艾米丽，让我们假设一下，民主党人最终能在这种双管齐下的程序上达成共识。

sentences.en: What about Republicans?
sentences.zh: 共和党人呢？

sentences.en: They must understand that passing the bipartisan infrastructure bill this week paves the way for Democrats to accomplish this longer wish list through the partisan budget reconciliation process,
sentences.zh: 他们一定明白，本周通过两党基础设施法案，为民主党人通过党派预算协调程序实现这个更长的愿望清单铺平了道路，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: And so how were they able to put that aside in voting to pass the infrastructure bill?
sentences.zh: 那么他们是如何在投票通过基础设施法案时将这一点搁置一旁的呢？

sentences.en: So I think it's a couple things.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为有几点原因。

sentences.en: I think that linkage is ultimately why more Republicans didn't support the bipartisan bill.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种联系最终是为什么没有更多共和党人支持两党法案的原因。

sentences.en: That was part of their argument for not voting for it.
sentences.zh: 这是他们不投票支持该法案的部分理由。

sentences.en: They kept calling it a Trojan horse because the second package was coming around the corner.
sentences.zh: 他们一直称其为“特洛伊木马”，因为第二个方案即将到来。

sentences.en: But I think also for the Republicans who did get on board, like Rob Portman, like Mitch McConnell,
sentences.zh: 但我认为，对于那些确实加入的共和党人，比如罗伯·波特曼，比如米奇·麦康奈尔来说，

sentences.en: ultimately the bipartisan infrastructure bill does have a lot of things they support.
sentences.zh: 两党基础设施法案最终确实包含了很多他们支持的内容。

sentences.en: And I think many of the members made a calculation that while in the minority trying to win back control of both chambers, they wanted to be able to point to some policy and say,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为许多成员做出了一个计算，即在作为少数党试图赢回两院控制权的同时，他们希望能够指出一些政策并说，

sentences.en: this is what I stand for.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所支持的。

sentences.en: This is the money I sent to you, my voters.
sentences.zh: 这就是我送给你们，我的选民的钱。

sentences.en: And say Democrats are successful with this expansive overhaul of the social safety net, this big sweeping package with all kinds of tax increases and changes.
sentences.zh: 如果民主党人成功地进行了这次社会安全网的全面改革，这个包含各种增税和变革的大规模方案，

sentences.en: For Republicans, they can then draw a really clear comparison between what they support and what they didn't.
sentences.zh: 对于共和党人来说，他们就可以在他们支持的和不支持的内容之间做出非常清晰的对比。

sentences.en: And that could be a pretty good argument for them in the election.
sentences.zh: 这对他们在选举中可能是一个很好的论点。

sentences.en: And it's given them a lot to work with politically.
sentences.zh: 这给了他们很多政治上的筹码。

sentences.en: You know, in that sense, this all feels like a pretty clever legislative maneuver by everyone involved to split these two processes up.
sentences.zh: 你知道，从这个意义上说，这一切感觉像是所有相关人员为了拆分这两个程序而采取的一种相当聪明的立法策略。

sentences.en: Yes, it's precarious, but it has also allowed for the process to get this far in the bipartisan manner that it has unfolded.
sentences.zh: 是的，这很危险，但也使得这一进程能够以目前所展现的两党合作方式走到这一步。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think a lot of people are surprised that there was a successful vote on the Senate floor, that they even reached the Senate floor.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为很多人对参议院能够成功投票，甚至能够进入参议院投票感到惊讶。

sentences.en: And I think it shows that this was one of the rare moments when the legislative and political incentives aligned across the Senate in both parties.
sentences.zh: 我认为这表明，这是参议院两党在立法和政治激励机制上达成一致的罕见时刻之一。

sentences.en: Infrastructure was always the most likely candidate for bipartisan support.
sentences.zh: 基础设施一直是最有可能获得两党支持的候选项目。

sentences.en: But I don't think you can discount the fact that it in part came about because Democrats decided they were going to go it alone with this typically partisan,
sentences.zh: 但我认为你不能忽视这样一个事实，即它在一定程度上是因为民主党人决定要独自进行这个通常是党派性的、

sentences.en: complicated process to pass as much as $3.5 trillion on their own and intentionally avoid the need for Republican votes.
sentences.zh: 复杂的程序，以独自通过高达3.5万亿美元的预算，并有意避免对共和党投票的需求。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: If you need a partisan process to get done the most likely candidate left for a bipartisan process, where does that leave you?
sentences.zh: 如果你需要一个党派程序来完成剩下的最有可能实现两党合作的候选项目，那你会处于什么境地？

sentences.en: I think it leaves you with a really significant moment this week in a deeply polarized Congress, but not necessarily a lot of prospects for bipartisanship in the future.
sentences.zh: 我认为这让你在本周这个极度两极分化的国会中处于一个非常重要的时刻，但不一定意味着未来会有很多两党合作的前景。

sentences.en: Thank you, Emily.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，艾米丽。

sentences.en: We appreciate your time.
sentences.zh: 感谢你的时间。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的事情。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, U.S.
sentences.zh: 周三，美国

sentences.en: health officials urged pregnant women to receive the vaccine against COVID-19,
sentences.zh: 卫生官员敦促孕妇接种新冠疫苗，

sentences.en: pointing to new data that found no increased risk of miscarriage for those who are immunized during the first 20 weeks of gestation.
sentences.zh: 指出新的数据显示，在怀孕前20周接种疫苗的人群中，流产风险并没有增加。

sentences.en: Previously, the officials had said that pregnant women could receive the vaccine.
sentences.zh: 此前，官员们曾表示孕妇可以接种疫苗。

sentences.en: Now, they say that those women should receive it.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们说这些女性应该接种。

sentences.en: And.
sentences.zh: 并且。

sentences.en: I spoke with Governor Cuomo yesterday, and he pledged his full support for a smooth transition.
sentences.zh: 我昨天与科莫州长进行了交谈，他承诺全力支持平稳过渡。

sentences.en: And I thanked him for his service to our state.
sentences.zh: 我感谢他为我们州所做的服务。

sentences.en: In her first public remarks since Governor Andrew Cuomo announced his resignation, New York's Lieutenant Governor, Kathy Hochul,
sentences.zh: 在安德鲁·科莫州长宣布辞职后的首次公开讲话中，纽约州副州长凯西·霍楚尔

sentences.en: said that it was time for the state to turn the page on the Cuomo era and that she was ready to replace him.
sentences.zh: 表示，现在是该州翻开科莫时代一页的时候了，她已经准备好接替他。

sentences.en: I believe it is appropriate and in the best interest of the state of New York.
sentences.zh: 我相信这是恰当的，也符合纽约州的最大利益。

sentences.en: And while it was not expected, it is a day for which I am prepared.
sentences.zh: 虽然这出乎意料，但我已经为此做好了准备。

sentences.en: Hochul, who will become New York's first female leader, vowed to change the culture of the governor's office, where sexual harassment was allegedly rampant.
sentences.zh: 即将成为纽约州首位女性领导人的霍楚尔誓言要改变州长办公室的文化，据称那里性骚扰猖獗。

sentences.en: At the end of my term, whenever it ends, no one will ever describe my administration as a toxic work environment.
sentences.zh: 在我任期结束时，无论何时结束，没有人会把我的政府描述为一个有毒的工作环境。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rob Zipko, Rachel Quester, Annie Brown, and Chelsea Daniel.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由Rob Zipko、Rachel Quester、Annie Brown和Chelsea Daniel制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Larissa Anderson and Paige Cowett, contains original music by Marion Lozano, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由Larissa Anderson和Paige Cowett编辑，包含Marion Lozano的原创音乐，并由Chris Wood进行工程处理。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严格控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
